status.note: Only meaningful inside a RadioGroup. Sourced from the W3C ARIA APG radio group pattern.

intent.purpose: One option in a radio group: a label that becomes the group's answer when chosen. It carries its own identity and its own disabled state, and nothing else — whether it is chosen is a comparison, not a property it holds.
behaviour: Compares its `value` against the group's selection to decide whether it is chosen. It cannot be told directly.
Chooses itself on click, and on Space when focused.
Cannot un-choose itself. Clicking the chosen option again does nothing, because a radio group always has exactly one answer.
Shows a mark inside its control when chosen, and nothing there when not.
Throws if rendered outside a RadioGroup. There is no selection to compare against, and looking unchosen would hide the mistake.
notFor: Use outside a RadioGroup. It has no fallback behaviour and deliberately fails loudly instead.
Being toggled off. If an option needs to be un-choosable, the set is not mutually exclusive and these are checkboxes.
Holding rich content. A radio's label is read as its accessible name, so anything structural inside it is announced as part of that name.

checked.description: Derived from the surrounding RadioGroup by comparing `value`. Not settable on this component.
checked.visual: A filled mark appears inside the control.

disabled.description: Set by the `disabled` prop or inherited from the group. Skipped by arrow-key movement.
disabled.visual: The label and control take the disabled colour and the pointer cursor is dropped.

hover.description: The pointer is over the option and it is not disabled.
hover.visual: The control's border takes its hover treatment.

focus-visible.description: Focused in a way the browser judges worth showing a ring for — keyboard, not a mouse click.
focus-visible.visual: A focus ring is drawn around the control.

a11y.keyboard: Reachable with Tab only when it is the group's current stop. Arrow keys on the group move here and choose in one action; Space chooses.
notes: The accessible name is whatever is passed as the label. An option given a non-text label has no name, and nothing here detects that.
The chosen state must not be carried by colour alone: the mark inside the control is what distinguishes chosen from unchosen for anyone who cannot separate the two colours.
`disabled` removes this option from arrow-key movement entirely, so a keyboard user cannot land on it to discover that it exists and is unavailable.

label.description: The option's name. Fills the `label` part.

root.description: The option: its control and its label, kept together so the whole row is the target.

control.description: The circle. Owns the focus ring and the border, and holds the mark that shows the option is chosen.

mark.description: The filled dot inside the control. Present only while chosen — it is the non-colour signal that this option is the answer.
